findings.reason: Removing the `validate_diagram` catalog row changes behaviour without anyone deciding it should. The profile gate fails closed on undeclared plugin tools (profile-gate.ts:110), so the read-only `validate_diagram` is now hidden from the `ask` and `brief` profiles. Before, it was declared 'read' and reachable there. The decision's reason (the tool is the `diagrams` project's, not this catalog's) does not match how this catalog treats other built-in envelopes: it still declares plugin rows for `ac-tools`, `spreadsheet-tools`, `endpoint-tools` and `ui-kit-component-tools` (`typeOp` with `contributedBy: 'plugin'`). `c4s-plugin-diagram` is also a built-in envelope shipped in the host package. The human should either confirm that losing diagram validation in ask/brief is intended, or keep a `typeOp('validate_diagram', …, 'read', true)` row declared on the envelope's behalf, as is done for the other envelopes.

The replacement e2e test no longer checks the host's half of the contract named in the file header: that the card is dispatched at runtime from the client plugin host once the app has booted. `body.innerText` not containing '<diagram' is also true when no card renders at all, for example when the prebuilt envelope's frontend bundle fails to load or register. Then nothing in this suite fails, even though the header says this is the thing under test. Add a host-level assertion that the generic `single_element` card for the diagram slug mounted (a figure/card node from the registered `renderCard`), without depending on how the envelope draws the SVG.

Two comments are now stale. The discovery-order rationale still says `plugins/<name>/dist` is gitignored build output that may be left over, but `plugins/c4s-plugin-diagram/dist/` is committed source of truth after this diff (it has a .gitignore exception). The module header (lines 5-7) also still lists tier (a) 'built-in direct' as a tier that exists, while `register-builtins.ts` and every call to it were deleted. Reword both so they describe the current two-tier layout and the committed prebuilt `dist/`.
